mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates the Federal Reserve is shifting to an easing stance, lowering discount rates and boosting equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals tightening monetary policy, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs indicates labor market strength, prompting firms to expand capital spending and boost earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in monthly employment growth below -10,000 jobs signals labor market weakness, prompting firms to reduce capital expenditures and earnings, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in contraction periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) above 1,000 units indicates growing consumer demand, prompting firms to raise capital expenditures and earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in retail sales below -500 units indicates weak consumer demand, prompting firms to cut capital expenditures and earnings, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in contraction periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 points indicates softening supply conditions, prompting firms to prioritize debt reduction and reduce earnings, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in contraction periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production above 200 points indicates strengthening supply conditions, prompting firms to expand capital expenditures and earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
